name: srgn
desc: Code surgeon for precise text and code transplantation
why: A code surgeon that matches and transforms code by syntax-aware grammar, a clever transform, though close to many refactoring tools.

brief.what_it_is: srgn is a command-line tool, written in Rust, that works like grep but understands source code syntax, and it can also change what it finds. You give it a scope, which can be a regular expression, a language-grammar scope such as 'all comments in Python' or 'struct definitions in Go', or both. You can then give it an action such as replacement, deletion, squeezing, casing changes, Unicode normalization, symbol substitution, or German umlaut fixing. Input comes from stdin or from files it walks recursively, and output is the matched lines in search mode or the transformed text otherwise. The README shows examples across C, C#, Go, HCL (Terraform), Python, Rust, and TypeScript.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says regular expressions and IDE tools such as 'Rename all' or 'Find all references' cannot reach some precise locations in code, such as only the Python class bodies or only the real Rust unsafe keyword, and srgn aims to complement them. Its stated design goal is simplicity: 'if you know regex and the basics of the language you are working with, you are good to go.'
brief.how_it_works: Language scopes are built on tree-sitter, and the README describes them as queries that work 'much like pattern matching against a tree data structure'. The language scope is applied first, and the regex then runs only inside the scoped pieces. Replacement is a positional argument placed last and separated by '--' so that a missing quote cannot make the tool recursive and destructive. Multiple scope flags are AND-ed left to right unless -j is given, which runs them independently and joins the results.

commands_seen.context: Basic replacement, similar to tr: the first positional argument is the regex scope and the argument after -- is the replacement.
Search mode (no actions given) limited to the Python class definitions, so 'age' inside function bodies is not matched.
Two language scopes given in sequence; they are AND-ed so only lines matching all criteria are returned.
The -j flag runs each scope independently and joins the results instead of intersecting them.
Deletion action (same flag name as tr) removing whatever the regex matches.
Squeezing action collapses repeats of the scoped characters into one occurrence.

commands_seen.cmd: cat gnu.py | srgn --titlecase --python 'doc-strings' '(?<!The )GNU ([a-z]+)' -- '$1: GNU 🐂 is not Unix'
commands_seen.context: Combines a Python docstring scope, a regex scope with lookbehind, a titlecase action, and a replacement that uses the $1 capture variable.
Symbols action replaces multi-character ASCII symbols with single Unicode counterparts; --invert reverses it.
Mass-converts print calls to logging.info; the anchors keep print_more from matching.
Removes all C# comments in one pass, then a second pass deletes the leftover blank-space-only lines.

brief.install_notes: Install with brew install srgn, or download a prebuilt binary from the GitHub releases page. Other routes the README lists are nix-shell -p srgn for nixpkgs, sudo port install srgn for MacPorts, and an AUR package for Arch Linux. cargo-binstall is the fastest Rust route, and it falls back to compiling from source if no binary exists for your platform. Compiling with cargo install srgn needs the Rust toolchain plus a C compiler: gcc on Linux, clang on macOS, and MSVC with the 'Desktop development with C++' workload on Windows. The README also gives a GitHub Actions snippet using cargo-binstall. Shell completion is set up by appending eval "$(srgn --completions zsh)" to ~/.zshrc for zsh. No accounts, API keys, or first-run configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: It puts a tree-sitter grammar scope in front of a regex, so you can ask for something like 'the regex only inside Python docstrings' or 'only Rust unsafe items' without writing a parser. Replacement is deliberately forced into a fixed position behind '--', so a forgotten quote can't turn the call into a destructive one.
brief.status: Maintained. The GitHub releases page lists v0.14.2 as the latest release, dated 22 Feb 2026, and the release before it was 0.14.1 on 9 Nov 2025 (tagged 21 Nov 2025). The README calls the project beta. I did not check commit history directly.
brief.caveats: The README says srgn is in beta (major version 0), so you should only process files you can restore with git, and it warns that the advanced regex features come without the usual safety and performance guarantees. Only seven languages are supported, and the README mentions that the set of symbols for the symbols action is limited. The German word list adds to binary size, and the README says it can be left out by compiling without the german feature. Replacement actions are a fixed set, so the tr-style character-list second argument is not available. The README warns that deletion and squeezing need an explicit scope. The homepage README was cut off at 40,000 characters, so I did not see the full help output, the custom query section in full, or the Rust library section. The brew formula's caveats were empty.
quotes: A `grep`-like tool which understands source code syntax and allows for manipulation in addition to search.
The answer to "What if `grep`, `tr`, `sed` and `tree-sitter` got really drunk one night and had a baby?"
Feel free to file an issue if your use case is not covered.
